# Advanced assessment blueprint
## A causal-methods course should assess analysis, argument and defence.
:::
::: {.lipps-section}
| Component | Weight | Required product |
|---|---:|---|
| Advanced R laboratory portfolio | 15% | Reproducible code, diagnostics and interpretation |
| DAG and identification assignment | 20% | Causal graph, adjustment set and identification defence |
| Causal analysis report | 25% | Standardisation/weighting or survival analysis with sensitivity checks |
| Target-trial protocol | 20% | Eligibility, strategies, time zero, outcome, estimand and emulation plan |
| Methods viva | 20% | Oral defence of assumptions, estimator, limitations and transportability |
:::
::: {.lipps-section}
## Minimum pass standard
A technically correct model cannot compensate for a mis-specified estimand. A learner who cannot distinguish prediction from causal inference, or cannot explain exchangeability/positivity/consistency for their analysis, has not yet demonstrated advanced epidemiological competence.
:::
